_comment: THE place to change models, tiers and budgets. After editing run: python scripts/agent/sync.py  (see docs/human/configuration.md)

architect._comment: Your main Claude Code session. sync.py writes `model` into .claude/settings.json. Set effort (e.g. high) in Claude Code itself.

executor._comment: Ticket field `difficulty` picks the tier. runner: claude-cli (headless `claude -p`, run by run_loop.py / run_executor.py), claude-subagent (spawned by the architect in its own session), or aider (local/any LiteLLM model).

claude_cli._comment: Command for runner claude-cli. {model}, {effort} and {max_turns} are substituted (an empty {effort} drops its flag); the prompt (instructions + pack) goes on stdin. The worker starts INSIDE its ticket worktree (.worktrees/<id>), with AGENT_TICKET=<id> set, so relative paths and the path guard just work. Add your stack tools to extra_allowed_tools.
claude_cli._extra_allowed_tools_comment: Stack commands headless workers may run, appended to --allowedTools. Proposed by the architect in Phase 0, e.g. ["Bash(cargo:*)"] or ["Bash(pytest:*)", "Bash(ruff:*)"].
claude_cli._command_prefixes_comment: Output wrappers your global CLAUDE.md asks agents to put in front of commands (e.g. rtk). For every allowed Bash(<cmd>:*) the same command behind each prefix is allowed too, e.g. Bash(rtk uv:*). Only listed commands, never Bash(rtk:*).
claude_cli._mirror_shells_comment: Every allowed Bash(<cmd>:*) rule is also allowed for these shell tools, e.g. PowerShell(uv:*). Claude Code on Windows often tries PowerShell first; without this, that call is denied and costs a turn.

executor._tiers_effort_comment: Tier `effort` is passed to headless workers as `claude --effort` and logged in usage. Empty = your Claude Code default.

tdd._comment: Tests first. A ticket with tdd on (default; `tdd: false` in a ticket turns it off with a reason) must commit its tests before any implementation: the worker runs `run_executor.py <id> --red`, which accepts only test files, commits them and requires the ticket's verify commands to FAIL. --finish refuses a ticket without that red commit.
tdd._test_command_patterns_comment: The red step only counts a FAILING TEST command: a verify command that names one of the ticket's test files or matches one of these regexes. A failing lint/format check never makes tests 'red'.

reviewer._comment: Run by scripts/agent/run_review.py (tickets) and run_pr_review.py (milestone PRs). The packet is sent on stdin ({prompt} via '-'), Codex runs read-only and only answers; the script writes the review file and applies the verdict. {model}, {effort} and {out_file} are substituted; an empty model drops its '-m' flag (CLI default). `hard` applies to tickets whose difficulty is in hard.difficulties and, if milestone_pr is true, to milestone PR reviews. Default routing: S/M tickets -> reviewer.model (fast model), L tickets and milestone PRs -> reviewer.hard.model (strongest model). Empty model = the CLI's own default from ~/.codex/config.toml, which sends every review to the same model.

auto_approve._comment: Skip the LLM review for tiny diffs that passed all gates. Off by default.

reviewer._diff_comment: Files matching generated_globs (top level) are listed with their line counts but their content is never sent.

loop._comment: scripts/agent/run_loop.py: runs worker -> gates -> review -> fix -> merge for every ready ticket without the architect. max_parallel: conflict-free tickets (no shared files_owned / lock_resources) run at the same time, each in its own worktree. Use 1 for a single-GPU local tier.

calibration._comment: First run of a milestone (no ticket integrated yet) stops after `tickets` finished tickets and prints a calibration report. The architect asks you about this in Phase 0.

verify._comment: Global gate commands run for every ticket (after the ticket's own verify list). Fill these from your stack profile.
verify._fix_commands_comment: Auto-fixers run in the ticket worktree BEFORE the gates (formatters, `lint --fix`), so a formatting slip never costs a whole worker run. {files} = the ticket's changed files that exist (quoted); without {files} the command runs as written. Python: ["uv run --frozen ruff format {files}", "uv run --frozen ruff check --fix-only {files}"].

_lock_resources_comment: Files that two parallel tickets must never both touch. Examples: Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, package-lock.json, migrations/**, Assets/Scenes/**, *.uproject
_generated_globs_comment: Lock files and other generated files. Agents see their NAMES (and size / changed-line counts) but never their content: packs list them without content, the reviewer gets only their line counts, and the read hook blocks Read on them. Change them with their tool (uv lock, npm install), never by hand.

read_guard._comment: Claude Code hook blocks whole-file reads of huge generated files (e.g. Unity YAML scenes).

git._comment: Ticket worktrees are real `git worktree`s checked out under worktree_dir inside the repo (gitignored); git keeps their metadata in .git/worktrees/.
